answer: Resistance should come from priced identity, not stricter filtering. Before any agent may attest, its kernel posts a bond into a shared vault; that bond is forfeited the instant two aliases are caught signing the same slot. Every signature joins one public ocean of records, so collusion surfaces as a replayable collision. Honest agents lose only the opportunity cost of locked capital, while an attacker must fund a separate bond per alias and lose all of them on first detection: faking n identities costs n bonds, not n minutes.
